label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/insecure-randomness): alert-TP — resolved sink value is rememberMeKey = Long.toString(new java.util.Random().nextLong()) at L72-L73. java.util.Random is a weak/predictable PRNG used to generate a security-sensitive remember-me token (authentication cookie value), which is then stored in HttpSession and set as a secure cookie. This matches the weak-randomness rule criteria. Alert 2 (java/xss): alert-unclear — the sink at L111-L116 prints rememberMe.getName() and rememberMe.getValue() to the HTTP response. These values originate from a Cookie object just created server-side with cookieName (class-name derived) and rememberMeKey (randomly generated), not from user-supplied input on this execution path. However, cookies are inherently user-controllable on subsequent requests, creating ambiguity about whether this represents a realistic XSS vector. Case TP driven by Alert 1 (insecure randomness feeding auth token).
